evidence: A DOE-funded SUNY-Buffalo project designed exactly this cycle — membrane sorbents regenerated by solar heating and loaded during electricity-free radiative cooling (5-7 C below ambient) — but only as materials work plus preliminary techno-economics, with no working tower demonstrated.

An ultrastable beta-carbonic anhydrase made by directed evolution (stable to ~107 C in 4.2 M amine) was demonstrated capturing CO2 from flue gas with a 25-fold absorption-rate enhancement, and enzymatic flue-gas capture is commercialised by Novonesis/Saipem; only the cement-kiln application and the structure-prediction-guided redesign were not found.

Electrochemical ocean alkalinity enhancement has been field-tested from shore (Ebb Carbon's bipolar-membrane prototype at Sequim, 47,000 gallons discharged) and MIT has proposed membrane-free electrochemical 'ocean-scrubbing' ships at lab scale, but no vessel-mounted electrochemical alkalinity system exists; the one ship-mounted ocean-CDR system in development (Calcarea) uses limestone, not electrodialysis.

Anti-uPAR senolytic CAR T cells improved metabolic health and exercise capacity in aged mice from a single dose (Nature Aging), but there is no human trial and nothing resembling an encapsulated implant with a valve for repeat dosing.

Closed-loop acoustic stimulation headbands that read forehead EEG and play phase-locked tones to amplify slow waves have been run at home for 14 nights in Alzheimer's patients, and multi-night trials are now testing waste clearance; only the glymphatic benefit and the sleep-position nudge are unproven.

Pulsed OSKM reprogramming in skin is established in mice — mosaic partial epidermal reprogramming healed wounds faster with less scarring including in diabetic conditions (Nature Communications, 2026), and intradermal AAV-OSK improved healing in aged mice — but delivery is genetic or viral and no microneedle patch with an on/off timer has been demonstrated.

A glucose-sensing E. coli Nissle 1917 (GIFT) using a HexR/KDPG switch to release GLP-1 only when blood sugar rises worked in mice and in diabetic monkeys (published in Nature), and constitutively GLP-1-secreting strains already cut body weight in diet-induced obese mice.

A centimetre-scale wireless optogenetic implant (Texas A&M, Nature Communications) delivers light-sensitive proteins to gastric vagal afferents via the nodose ganglion and drives satiety with LEDs in mice; only the human version is missing.

Local cooling of supraclavicular brown fat by gel-pack patch, Peltier element or phase-change vest is patented and sold commercially, and a stretchable thermoelectric skin patch holding skin at 32 C was demonstrated (Science Advances, 2019), but no electrocaloric wearable exists and none of the solid-state devices has been shown to activate brown fat.

Composites that locate a crack by the resistance change of an embedded carbon-nanotube network and then heal it have been demonstrated since RPI's 2007 work (70% strength recovery), with a 2024 microcapsule-plus-MWCNT epoxy reaching 90% healing efficiency; the gap is flight qualification, not the mechanism.

Prysmian's SUPERSEAL sells pressure-triggered self-healing sealant in cable insulation, but for low-voltage direct-burial cable, and SINTEF's microcapsule healing of electrical trees is only proposed for subsea connectors; no deep-water pressure-cured repair layer backed by a graphene barrier has been demonstrated.

PNNL's SLIC is a nontoxic superhydrophobic lubricant-infused composite coating that is explicitly self-healing and antifouling, benchmarked against a leading commercial foul-release hull coating on surface energy, roll-off angle, abrasion and primer adhesion; Michigan's self-healing F-POSS polyurethane does the same healing trick by molecular migration.

NASA screened 64 hydrogen-storing MOFs and metal hydrides as radiation shielding (10% beat HDPE in solar-particle simulations) and a 2025 EPJ Plus study extended this to galactic cosmic rays, with ESA flagging MOF powder handling as the barrier, but all of it is simulation and no shielding wall has been built or flown.

Dsup delivered as lipid-encased mRNA halved radiation damage in human epithelial cells and was demonstrated in vivo as a radioprotectant before radiotherapy (Nature Biomedical Engineering, 2025), on top of earlier work showing ~40% less X-ray damage in Dsup-expressing human cells; bone marrow targeting specifically was not found.

MOFs with size- and charge-matched pores (crown-ether-walled MOF-18Cr6 at 99.7% removal, a 2025 Cu-MOF with ultra-high Sr selectivity against large excesses of Ca and Ba) exist only as wastewater separation studies, while oral strontium decorporation has been shown in animals only with alginate and Zn-InsP6; no MOF has been tested as a gut-binding pill.

Human iPSC-derived cells injected into SIX1/SALL1-knockout pig blastocysts produced humanised mesonephros (early kidney) structures to embryonic day 28 — the first solid human-like organ grown in another species — though the organ is part-pig and far from transplantable.

Functional isogenic thymic organoids from human pluripotent stem cells support T-cell development, express AIRE and generate regulatory T cells (2023), and implanted iPSC-derived thymic organoids selected human T cells and cut tumour burden in humanised mice (Cancer Research Communications, 2025); immune rejuvenation in old humans is untested.

Projector-driven optogenetics has already printed spatiotemporal gene-expression patterns onto organoids, including local SHH activation in one pole of a neural organoid (Nature Methods, 2023), and muPatternScope added image-guided closed-loop patterning in which measured cell patterns steer the next light pattern (Nature Communications, 2024).

Lanmodulin-family proteins fixed in chromatography columns separated neodymium from dysprosium to >98% individual purity in a single stage, and engineered binding proteins recovered Nd and Dy from simulated NdFeB magnet leachate with >200-fold inter-lanthanide selectivity.

Selective-membrane electrodialysis on spent-battery leachate produced a 99% Li-pure retentate with 68.8% retention and LiOH via a bipolar stage (Environmental Science & Technology, 2024), and MOF subnanometre-pore membranes already sieve Li from Mg and Na at high selectivity in scaled modules.

Tracer-based sorting with fluorescent markers compounded into the resin is established (reviewed in Polymers 2022), silicon quantum-dot tracers are patented (EP3870639) and an EU project is piloting lifetime-coded Si quantum dots for >99% sorting purity; reading accumulated melt cycles from the tracer is the one part not demonstrated.

Engineered PET hydrolases already depolymerise the polyester in poly-cotton without melting it — a Humicola insolens cutinase gave up to 30% terephthalic acid from high-crystallinity PET/cotton under moist-solid conditions while the cotton was recovered, and the 2025 PET2-14M-6Hot variant beat LCC-ICCG on 65/35 PET/cotton at moderate temperature.

Mealworms living on polystyrene and the causal role of their gut bacteria are well demonstrated (Exiguobacterium sp. YT2, Klebsiella sp. WJ2020 at 4.35% and Cellulosimicrobium at 6.93% film loss over 60 days), but no engineered gut symbiont carrying added plastic-degrading genes, and no feed-safety demonstration, was found.

Films with the depolymerase compounded in at manufacture and held dormant by a protective shell until warmth and moisture release it are built: UC Berkeley's enzyme nanoparticles with random-heteropolymer shells survive melt processing and degrade the film on a hot-water trigger without microplastics, and an engineered PLA depolymerase at 0.02% w/w fully disintegrated film under home-compost conditions in 20-24 weeks (Nature, 2024); only the tardigrade-protein shell material is unexplored.

The pieces exist separately — fluoroionophore-based implanted potassium optical sensors are patented, fluorescent dermal tattoo sensors with crown-ether dyes are read transdermally by a smartphone plus filters, and a Fraunhofer/Ki'tech subcutaneous potassium monitor reached smartphone-readout proof of concept in 2025 — but no implanted engineered fluorescent protein potassium sensor read through the skin by phone camera was found.
